text:
Alexander Wennberg had 55 points for San Jose last season. This one keeps getting interrupted. The Sharks' alternate captain missed about three weeks from mid-October before the team activated him on Nov. 9 (Pro Hockey Rumors reported the move), sat out again Nov. 14, and was back Tuesday, when Max Miller of Sharks Hockey Digest noted he had yet to take a faceoff.

He's still playing over 20 minutes a night, but the production hasn't followed: no goals on 17 shots, three assists, and pointless in four straight with the chances thinning out. Our numbers call it some of each, a few fewer looks and nothing going in.

The five-on-five picture is the concern. San Jose has taken 39% of the expected goals (the quality of chances) with him on. That isn't his usual profile: Evolving-Hockey had him in the 85th percentile among forwards at taking chances away last season, plus 2.5 goals from drawing more penalties than he took. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking says he carries the puck in on 60% of his entries and makes 22% of his setups from behind the net. Watch whether that game returns.
